scope: Code-review follow-up on the uncommitted common-components candidate (CLI/bundle 0.10.0, Rust SDK 0.4.0, UI 1.1.0, core schema 23). Source changes and isolated checks only.

review.method: Static review of the working tree against a5d714f, then each finding compared with the code before it was changed.

fixes.finding: A failed or interrupted upload left the internal uploading state, and every later PUT for that reservation answered 409 while the API and UI still offered to send again.
fixes.change: An upload may start from pending or uploading until the reservation expires. The row lock, not the status, excludes a second upload. Leftover part bytes and a blob whose ready commit did not happen are removed at the start of the next attempt; the part is removed when an attempt fails.

fixes.finding: Reservation, attach, cancel and upload opened a transaction (the global reservation lock or a file row lock), then ran df and took a second pooled connection for an authorization recheck. With a pool of ten, concurrent requests could leave every connection held by a transaction waiting for another connection.
fixes.change: Disk space is measured before the transaction. Reservation, attach, cancel and detach recheck authorization immediately before a short transaction and take no second connection inside it. Only the recheck after an upload transfer still does, bounded by the four transfer slots. A state change that meets a running upload waits five seconds and answers 409 file_upload_in_progress instead of holding a connection for the whole transfer.

fixes.finding: Every reservation first swept elapsed and cancelling files of all installations and propagated any removal error, so one file that could not be removed made every app's reservation fail, repeatedly, on the same row.
fixes.change: Housekeeping moved to a worker task that runs about once a minute. It pages past a file whose removal fails and reports it. Elapsed reservations stop counting toward quota and report expired at once, so quota does not depend on when housekeeping runs.

fixes.finding: Common UI created request and client IDs with crypto.randomUUID, which does not exist in an app frame served over internal HTTP.
fixes.change: requestId() in the common UI uses crypto.getRandomValues. Files, sharing and the representative app use it.

fixes.finding: ShareEditor gave a newly added subject the first listed role, and the SDK listed roles alphabetically: editor for the representative app, owner for an owner/reader app.
fixes.change: The SDK lists roles in declared order and names defaultRole only when exactly one role is the least (its actions are a subset of every other role's and it cannot manage sharing). ShareEditor preselects only that role; otherwise the person must choose a role before saving.

fixes.finding: The Docker-runtime preview bound its backend listener to the bridge gateway address, which is not a host address with Docker Desktop or a rootless engine, so the whole preview could fail to start.
fixes.change: When that address cannot be bound the preview starts with the listener on loopback and without backend platform calls, and prints a notice. Not reproduced: this host is Linux with a native engine; only the fallback selection is unit tested.

fixes.finding: The untyped platformApi("directory") and platform_api("directory") calls now return a first page of at most 50 entries and cannot continue it.
fixes.change: Without a query these calls fail with directory_page_incomplete when more entries exist. Typed directory reads are unchanged. Apps on an older SDK still receive the first page from the server.

fixes.finding: No API released an attached file, so the per-installation quota only ever grew.
fixes.change: POST .../platform/files/{file}/detach with the attached reference deletes the bytes and returns the quota; cancel still refuses attached files. Rust SDK files_detach. The representative app does not use it yet.

fixes.finding: The SDK accepted uppercase UUIDs but compared them byte for byte with Core's lowercase answers (group membership, file ID, group grants).
fixes.change: Group membership and file ID comparisons ignore ASCII case; group IDs in grants are stored in lowercase.

fixes.finding: Housekeeping of other installations' files was audited under whichever user made the next reservation.
fixes.change: file.expired and file.cancelled written by housekeeping have no actor.

fixes.finding: Successful GETs were audited when the request path contained /files/ or /connections/ anywhere, including app API and artifact paths.
fixes.change: The matched route template decides which successful reads are audited.

fixes.finding: In the representative app a create request that never reached the server kept the form locked: the lookup could only say the result was unknown.
fixes.change: When the lookup shows nothing was created, the same request can be sent again under its original ID or cancelled, for projects and tasks.

fixes.finding: DirectoryPicker read the directory on every keystroke; each read is authorized and audited by the server.
fixes.change: Typing reads once after a 250 ms pause. Opening the list reads at once.

fixes.finding: Acl::require, sharing and replacement_result held a pooled connection and the resource lock across the Core directory call (up to 15 seconds).
fixes.change: They read the grants in a short transaction and return the connection before the directory call. require_in, replace_in and create_resource_in still call the directory inside the caller's transaction, which the lock they provide requires.

fixes.finding: The file gateway repeated the JSON gateway's admission checks, and the Storage route list existed separately in Core and in the CLI preview proxy.
fixes.change: Both gateways call runtime::app_target; Core admission, the preview endpoint and the CLI proxy use storage_contract::allowed_route.
